newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares/loans results seen unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares/loans results seen unchanged.

text.p: Russia has no plans to amend the results of last year's controversial auctions under the shares-for-loans scheme, a spokeswoman for First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin said on Monday.

Key players in the auctions, in which stakes in privatised companies were tendered in exchange for loans to the government, agreed last Friday the results would not be reviewed, spokeswoman Larisa Zelkova said.

The round table talks included representatives of Russia's Security Council, the Finance Ministry, the State Duma lower house of parliament, the parliamentary audit chamber, three banks -- Menatep, Rossiisky Kredit and Alfa-Bank and oil firms Sidanko and Yukos.

The auctions, which were designed to plug holes in the 1995 budget late in the year, were highly contentious. Winners were often closely associated with the auction organisers and the winning bids were frequently close to the starting price.
Under the original terms of the auctions, winners had to hang on to their shares until September 1 and could then sell them, keeping 30 percent of the proceeds and paying 70 percent into the budget.
However, Security Council Secretary Alexander Lebed wrote to President Boris Yeltsin asking for the period in which winners had to hold the shares to be extended until March 1, 1997.
In response, Yeltsin told Lebed and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to resolve the issue and come up with proposals by October 1, a government source said.
Lebed had said the shares had been sold at far below their real value.
Privatisation Minister Alfred Kokh, speaking before his appointment, said on September 4 he had no plans to extend the period in which auction winners had to hold the shares.
The scheme brought in some 4.7 trillion roubles last year.
Officials have said the era of mass privatisation is over and that the government will concentrate on fewer projects to raise 12 some trillion roubles this year.

Russia plans to hold an investment tender, open to foreign investors, for 15 percent of oil company Sibneft on October 25. The minimum price for the shares is 65.04 billion roubles and the minimum investment is $33.56 million, according to the Federal Property Fund's Reforma bulletin.
ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK) and Stolichny Bank Sberezhenii won the right to manage a 51 percent stake in Sibneft in a shares-for-loans auction late last year.
